subject: Concurrency budget, streaming requirements, and fallback plan for ACME POC
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Shah <priyanka@acme.com>, Carlos Mendez <carlos@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Concurrency budget, streaming requirements, and fallback plan for ACME POC

Hi Priyanka / Carlos — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we have alignment on performance targets and the options we'll exercise to meet them.

Recap of ask (as we heard it)
- Primary SLO: conversational latency p95 <= 250ms for single-turn text generation (non-streaming).
- Streaming mode: first token to client within 100ms; subsequent tokens steady-state <= 50ms/token when possible.
- Concurrency: sustained ~60 concurrent request slots during normal traffic, short bursts up to ~300 concurrent for 5–12 minutes.
- Throughput: baseline 120 QPS sustained at peak region.
- Quality target: match current vendor outputs for intent classification and entity extraction; we can validate with a 500-sample prompt set.

Cost/perf levers we discussed (brief)
- Continuous batching: trade throughput for latency; configure max batch wait to stay within p95 SLO.
- KV/prefix caching: cache common conversation prefixes to avoid re-generating early tokens.
- Quantization profiles: int8 (lowest impact on latency), 4-bit (cost savings, more model-specific regressions).
- Model variants + fallbacks: primary model for quality, smaller model (3B) as emergency fallback for extreme spikes; canary rollout between variants.
- Autoscale + reserved concurrency buckets: reserve a pool for premium users to guarantee latency during bursts.

Action items / ask of Acme
1) Send a sample traffic profile (1 week) showing request arrival distribution and a 500-record sample prompt set we can use for perf validation.
2) Confirm acceptable p95 target for streaming (is 250ms p95 single-turn + 100ms to first token for streaming acceptable?).
3) Provide a test service account and a list of endpoints we should hit for the perf run.

What Redwood will do next
- Neha and Rishi will draft a perf plan that tests: steady-state throughput, burst scenarios, streaming first-token latency, and KV cache hit effects.
- I will attach a mutual action plan and perf test instructions for you to review (first draft attached).
- We'll provide a rough cost delta between int8 and 4-bit quantization after the initial runs.

Proposed perf run window: May 12–13 (we can shift if you have procurement gating).

Thanks — if any of this is off, call it out and we'll update.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Concurrency budget, streaming requirements, and fallback plan for ACME POC

Ben — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming the high-level constraints from our side and a couple of clarifying notes: 

Confirmed targets
- Single-turn p95 target: 250ms (we can accept up to 275ms during short bursts if necessary, but prefer mitigation).
- Streaming: 100ms to first token is our goal; if steady-state drifts >60ms/token that will degrade UX noticeably.
- Sustained concurrency: 60; peak burst up to 300 for 5–10 minutes (we've seen spikes for flash promotions).

Additional context
- Quality: our content includes structured receipts and small tables; hallucination tolerance is low for entity fields. We'll provide 500 sample prompts covering the worst-case extraction cases.
- Security/compliance: PII in prompts is possible; we'll redact or provide test data. SOC2 docs and an IP addendum are in procurement queue.
- Procurement timeline: aiming for contract signature by end of June; technical validation (POC) must complete by mid-June.

Requests from Redwood
- Please include rough ESTIMATES of monthly cost delta for 1M generated tokens using int8 vs 4-bit (ballpark is fine).
- Can you commit to a perf window on May 12–13? We'll create a perf service account and share credentials by May 7.

Thanks — copying Carlos who owns engineering schedule.

—Priyanka

Subject: Re: Concurrency budget, streaming requirements, and fallback plan for ACME POC

Thanks — a couple of technical clarifications from the perf/infra side and proposed test knobs we'll exercise: 

Test knobs and rationale
- Quantization: we'll run both int8 (GPTQ/OMP friendly) and 4-bit (GPTQ/QAT as available) profiles. Expectation: int8 will give ~1.6–2x cost reduction vs fp16 with minor latency improvements; 4-bit can push cost ~2.5–3x down but will need careful quality checks on extraction tasks.
- Continuous batching: set a maximum batch_wait_ms of 8–12ms for normal traffic; increase to 20–30ms only during sustained throughput tests to observe tail effects. We'll measure p50/p95/p99.
- KV/prefix caching: implement a 1M-entry LRU cache for the POC (we'll simulate cache-hit ratios 10%/30%/50% to show benefits).
- Model variants & fallback: primary: rwd-stable-7b (quantized profile), standby: rwd-stable-13b (higher quality profile but more expensive), emergency fallback: rwd-lite-3b. We'll validate semantic parity on the 500-sample set.
- Streaming: instrument first-byte latency and inter-token latency. For streaming, we will test both chunked output (token buffer size = 8) and greedy immediate emission.

Operational controls
- Reserve 20 concurrent slots as "premium" with latency isolation (these map to dedicated worker queues).
- Canary policy: start 5% traffic to new config, 25% after green metrics for 10 minutes, then full rollout. Automatic rollback on 3 consecutive p95 regressions > 10%.

Ask of Acme for technical validation
- 500-sample prompt set (masked PII OK) and a small labeled ground-truth for entity extraction.
- Expected 99th-percentile acceptable latency threshold for premium users (we'll use 350ms as default).

I'll draft a perf plan and a test script set and upload to the shared drive. If this looks good I'll schedule the perf run for May 12–13.

—Neha Kapoor
Sr. Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
